seasonal-hare-match.kind: Original labelled teaching model using bounded checked source facts.
givenFacts: Original spoken model cards describe a northern snowshoe-hare population whose coats are mostly brown during summer and mostly white during winter; not every population or individual is claimed identical.

Summer model background is brown ground/vegetation; winter model background is snow-covered. A hare matching a background can be harder for predators to see. These are original labelled teaching cases using checked biological facts, not original field photographs or observed pupil data.
The coat changes gradually by moult, with day length as a cue. It does not immediately recolour on touching snow or because a hare decides to match. No endocrine mechanism is a learner gate.
Transfer card: wintercolour has changed but snow is late, leaving brown ground. The white coat may stand out; camouflage success depends on the actual background.
seasonal-hare-match.question: Compare the same kind of hare across the seasonal cards: what changes in appearance, and how does the changed coat help on its corresponding background? Explain the seasonal response by connecting appearance, background and hiding from predators; simply naming winter/summer or white/brown is insufficient. Predict how the white winter coat works in the late-snow transfer. Would touching a brown patch instantly change the coat? Explain using the supplied gradual-change fact.
seasonal-hare-match.expectedEvidence: Actual appearance difference plus supported seasonal-function explanation; correct mismatch transfer. No requirement to name hormone, describe natural selection or add migration/hibernation repertoire. Do not infer whole AnimalCamouflage mastery from one seasonal organism; retain existing threeexample evidence and separate definition/function assessment.
seasonal-hare-match.nearMiss: A named object, copied authored model, single-condition match or memorised fact omits the required independent comparison, performance or supported explanation. Do not award complete source-task evidence for it.
seasonal-hare-match.changedCase: Compare the same kind of hare across the seasonal cards: what changes in appearance, and how does the changed coat help on its corresponding background? Predict how the white winter coat works in the late-snow transfer. Would touching a brown patch instantly change the coat? Explain using the supplied gradual-change fact.
seasonal-hare-match.attributionLimits: Original hypothetical model, not field data or actual learner evidence. Complete contributor assessment remains separate.

daily-seasonal-school-nature-plans.kind: original stipulated comparison, not an event record
givenFacts: A hypothetical class does TWO actual outdoor activities: nature observation/drawing and reading together outside. It compares the SAME activities across declared adult-approved safe morning/afternoon/evening and four-season conditions; no independent child night outing is assigned. Both activities remain physically outdoors for the required enabling-innovation comparisons.

Four separate safe-weather example cards at this model site: cool spring light rain; warm sunny summer; cool autumn light rain with an ordinary moderate breeze and earlier darkness; cold winter with snow nearby but an adult-cleared accessible dry observation/reading area and suitable brief supervised conditions. These are explicitly selected safe conditions, not every day of a season or a child weather-exposure protocol.

OUTDOOR innovation cards: suitable waterproof layers and a rain cover keep light rain off people and reading/drawing materials; adjustable insulating layers retain body warmth in cold; a well-positioned shade canopy reduces solar warming of the outdoor area; an adult-approved windbreak in the stipulated moderate breeze helps protect the outdoor reading/drawing area. Match and explain appropriate outdoor choices across ALL FOUR safe seasonal cards and both activities. None guarantees safety in severe weather.

School service cards explicitly stipulate that adults change outdoor lesson times, clear an approved route after snow, and move the class indoors if weather is unsafe. No actual school schedule, real clearance result or energy-saving figure is asserted.

An enclosed shelter with adult-operated heating is explicitly an INDOOR alternative. Moving inside can be a sensible plan if needed, but it does not demonstrate continuing an OUTDOOR activity across the year and cannot replace the required outdoor comparisons.
daily-seasonal-school-nature-plans.question: Compare morning and afternoon/evening effects on the SAME human activity: what changes and why? For BOTH outdoor nature observation/drawing AND outdoor reading, compare ALL FOUR declared safe seasonal conditions. Identify suitable outdoor rain/warm-layer/shade/wind-protection innovations, explain which relevant problem each helps with and one limit. Keep the activities physically outdoors; a single coat match or moving every activity into a heated room is insufficient. Assemble a sensible weather kit for rain, heat/sun and cold, explaining choices and how conditions affect the activity. Transfer: a cool summer day or mild winter day requires the actual conditions to govern the choice, not the season name. Explain which school/community service changes in the model and who benefits or faces difficulty. If the designated outdoor route is inaccessible or weather is unsafe, revise the plan with an adult instead of treating the innovation as a guarantee. Changed case: a class proposes doing all winter and rainy-day nature observation/reading only inside the enclosed heated shelter. Explain why this may be a sensible indoor alternative but DOES NOT answer how innovations can maintain the outdoor activities in the declared safe conditions; give suitable actual outdoor choices as well. Severe weather/accessibility can still require postponement or moving inside without counting that as outdoor evidence.
daily-seasonal-school-nature-plans.expectedEvidence: For BOTH named outdoor activities, daily AND all four seasonal timing comparisons; actual OUTDOOR enabling innovations/functions/limits and changed indoor-only near miss; condition-matched kit reasons/transfer; supported people/service consequences.
daily-seasonal-school-nature-plans.nearMiss: A named object, copied authored model, single-condition match or memorised fact omits the required independent comparison, performance or supported explanation. Do not award complete source-task evidence for it.
daily-seasonal-school-nature-plans.changedCase: Assemble a sensible weather kit for rain, heat/sun and cold, explaining choices and how conditions affect the activity. Transfer: a cool summer day or mild winter day requires the actual conditions to govern the choice, not the season name. Changed case: a class proposes doing all winter and rainy-day nature observation/reading only inside the enclosed heated shelter. Explain why this may be a sensible indoor alternative but DOES NOT answer how innovations can maintain the outdoor activities in the declared safe conditions; give suitable actual outdoor choices as well. Severe weather/accessibility can still require postponement or moving inside without counting that as outdoor evidence.
daily-seasonal-school-nature-plans.attributionLimits: No PE skills, training or fitness content. Source outdoor activity is environmental/science observation. No clinical/dose/weather-exposure advice; adults use normal school safety/access arrangements. No learner must control a heater, clear snow, go out at night or physically tolerate dangerous weather. BuildingShade whole mastery remains actual design/build/test/iteration; describing this canopy card is not that performance.

daily-seasonal-living-environment.kind: original six-cell consequence comparison using bounded checked biological facts
givenFacts: Daily living-things card: a specifically described northern insect-eating bat roosts by day and comes out around dusk to drink and forage. This is a bounded example, not all bats everywhere or a child wildlife-handling activity.

Daily physical-environment card: one unobstructed location gets daylight and solar warming input during day; after sunset no DIRECT sunlight reaches that location. Real ground/air may retain heat, and clouds/other heat sources matter; darkness does not instantly freeze or cool everything.

Seasonal living-things cards reuse the checked selected snowshoe-hare appearance case and a selected temperate deciduous maple losing leaves in autumn, contrasted with a selected evergreen pine retaining needles. The maple is not dead merely because it is leafless; not every tree follows the same pattern.

Seasonal physical-environment card: the selected northern temperate model has longer daylight and generally more incoming solar energy in summer, shorter daylight and less in winter; four-season light/heating comparison is explicitly supplied in the solar case. Actual daily weather can depart from the usual seasonal tendency.

Society/people cells use the explicitly stipulated school plans/services from daily-seasonal-school-nature-plans. The six cells are DAILY people/services, DAILY physical environment, DAILY natural living things; SEASONAL people/services, SEASONAL physical environment, SEASONAL natural living things.
daily-seasonal-living-environment.question: For EACH of the six supplied cells, explain a timing→consequence connection; do not merely list seasons, animals or clothing. Compare how a bat daily activity pattern and a hare seasonal appearance response relate to different timescales. Describe what changes, how it affects meeting needs/hiding, and what remains unknown from the cards. Transfer: a winter day at the selected site is unusually mild and snow is late. Which usual expectations are unreliable now? Keep the continuing seasonal/daylight cycle distinct from that day’s weather.
daily-seasonal-living-environment.expectedEvidence: Connected actual accounts across society, environment and natural living things and both daily/seasonal timescales; supported contrasts and changedcondition application.
daily-seasonal-living-environment.nearMiss: A named object, copied authored model, single-condition match or memorised fact omits the required independent comparison, performance or supported explanation. Do not award complete source-task evidence for it.
daily-seasonal-living-environment.changedCase: Transfer: a winter day at the selected site is unusually mild and snow is late. Which usual expectations are unreliable now? Keep the continuing seasonal/daylight cycle distinct from that day’s weather.
daily-seasonal-living-environment.attributionLimits: No bat-topic mastery, all-bat hibernation, population estimates, local species census or climate attribution inferred. These are model cases, not field datasets or actual child observations. Complete seasonal/yearly observation repertoire in existing guides remains separately required when assessing those topics.

solar-day-four-season-comparison.kind: original qualitative controlled model plus actual-observation protocol; no fabricated measured dataset
givenFacts: DAY model at one selected northern temperate site, clear unobstructed conditions: early morning low sunlight, around solar noon higher incoming solar intensity, late afternoon lower intensity, after sunset no direct sunlight. This describes incoming solar input, NOT a rule that air or ground is hottest exactly at noon.

FOUR-SEASON model at the same site: spring daylight is lengthening; summer has the longest daylight and generally stronger/more daily solar input; autumn daylight is shortening; winter has the shortest daylight and generally less solar input. Compare spring and autumn as intermediate patterns, not an asserted identical measured temperature.

Qualitative heating-model cards use the SAME material, equal starting conditions, same fixed exposure duration and no other heat source: more incoming solar input provides greater warming opportunity; less provides less. A cloudy summer card can have lower measured surface warming than a clear winter card. No numerical readings or real weather records are invented.

Actual-observation materials: adult-approved matched non-hot safe samples, relative thermometer/temperature strip, record sheet and safe shaded/unshaded area. At available morning/noon/afternoon sessions record starting/ending relative warmth, sun/shade/cloud conditions and elapsed comparison period. Read thermometer rather than touch potentially hot ground or equipment; do not stare at or look through materials toward the Sun.

Seasonal observation record is an explicit delivery task: compare actual daylight-at-known-times observations across the year (or checked attributed records supplied by the teacher), recording source/time/conditions. Do not label the qualitative model cards as these actual observations.
solar-day-four-season-comparison.question: Describe BOTH the light and heating-input patterns across a day and all FOUR seasons using the separate resources; a sun-vs-shade pair or summer/winter-only answer is insufficient. Explain what the actual sample observations do and do not show. If cloud/wind affects a session, record it and avoid forcing it to fit the model. Predict the cloudy-summer/clear-winter contrast. Can one measurement prove winter has more daylight or that the Sun never warms things in winter? Why not? For SunlightWarms contributor evidence separately conduct an actual matched sunlight/shade leave-and-revisit observation and report relative changes and source-of-warming reasoning. For annual daylight contributor evidence separately use the actual/attributed record, not a memorised season label.
solar-day-four-season-comparison.expectedEvidence: Day and all four seasonal relative light+solar warming descriptions; explicit incoming-energy vs stored ambient warmth distinction; changedweather transfer. Actual contributor observations are recorded when delivered rather than invented in authoring.
solar-day-four-season-comparison.nearMiss: A named object, copied authored model, single-condition match or memorised fact omits the required independent comparison, performance or supported explanation. Do not award complete source-task evidence for it.
solar-day-four-season-comparison.changedCase: Predict the cloudy-summer/clear-winter contrast. Can one measurement prove winter has more daylight or that the Sun never warms things in winter? Why not?
solar-day-four-season-comparison.attributionLimits: DOE source has overbroad noon/equinox passages: use only time/day/season/weather dependence and qualitative solar-noon input; no exact equal 12-hour/equinox dates/overhead Ontario assertions. No degrees, clocks arithmetic, solar-angle calculations or axial-tilt mechanism are added to the descriptive E2.3 gate. This task does not certify causal E2.1.
